//: The version is written to the ROOT package.json, not to packages/angulux/package.json.
That is not a stylistic choice: tools/build/build-helper.mjs updatePackageJson() assigns
`pkg.version = <root>.version` on every build, so a version written into the package
manifest is silently reverted by the next prebuild. Targeting packages/angulux here
produced a pipeline that tagged a release and published nothing, with a green run.
Root is private:true, so npmPublish stays false and nothing is published from here —
the workflow publishes packages/angulux/dist explicitly, under OIDC.
There is deliberately no @semantic-release/git here, and therefore no changelog file.
That plugin commits the version bump and pushes it to `main`, which is a protected
branch: `Changes must be made through a pull request` and `Required status check CI is
expected`. The second condition is unsatisfiable by construction — the release commit
carries [skip ci], so it never gets a CI run to satisfy the check with.
semantic-release's own push is `git push --tags <url>` — tags only, no branch ref — so
without this plugin nothing in a release touches `main` at all. The git tag and the
GitHub release (which carries the same generated notes) are the record.
Consequence: the version in the root package.json on `main` stays at whatever was last
committed by hand and is NOT the released version. Nothing reads it as one —
semantic-release derives the next version from the tags, and the build stamps dist from
the root manifest as written during prepare, inside the same run.
commit-analyzer and release-notes-generator are wrapped by ./release/rail-filter.mjs.
The path gate in release.yml decides whether this train RUNS; it never filtered the
commits, so once a train ran it analysed every commit since its own tag. Measured
2026-08-14: both trains printed `Analysis of 17 commits complete` — the same seventeen.
That published a changelog crediting each train with work that is not in it. The wrapper
hands both plugins only the commits that touched this train, from the path list in
release/rails.mjs, which release.yml reads too — one definition, so the gate and the
filter cannot come to cover different things.
ONE entry, not two. The wrapper exports BOTH analyzeCommits and generateNotes, so the
two plugins it replaced collapse into a single list item carrying both configurations.
Listing it twice — which is how it first shipped, because two plugins were replaced
one-for-one — makes semantic-release run generateNotes twice and CONCATENATE the
output: the 22.2.1 release notes were published with every entry printed twice, once
under the default section names and once under the presetConfig ones. The version was
unaffected (both passes agree, and the highest release type wins), so nothing failed.
check:release-plugins now refuses a duplicated plugin path.
